artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, let $D(P)$ denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of points of $P$, i.e., $D(P) = |\{\,\|p-q\| : p,q \in P,\ p \neq q\,\}|$. A family $\{P_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ of planar point sets with $|P_n|=n$ is called near-optimal if $D(P_n) = O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ as $n \to \infty$. Known examples of near-optimal families include the $\sqrt{n}\times\sqrt{n}$ section of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and the triangular lattice. 

Give a structural characterization of all near-optimal planar point sets. In particular, decide whether every near-optimal set must in some precise sense possess "lattice structure", and identify the necessary and sufficient geometric/combinatorial conditions on $P_n$ that force $D(P_n) = O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing near-optimal point sets for the Erdős distinct distances problem (and Erdős's question of whether every such set has "lattice structure") remains open. Partial results are known—e.g., every near-optimal set must contain a line with Ω(log n) points, and for any 0<α≤1/4 must contain a line or circle with n^α points—but no full characterization has been established.
